raw_text:
Below is a 12-week, phased general strength program tailored to a 42-year-old male desk worker with prior L4–L5 disc herniation (now asymptomatic) and the constraints: no heavy spinal loading and no loaded spinal flexion. Emphasis is on neutral-spine control, hip-dominant patterns, unilateral work, machines and cables, tempo/control, and progressive overload without axial compression. Program is 3 days/week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri). Add optional low-impact cardio and mobility on non-lifting days.

Key principles
- Spine safety: Neutral spine throughout; avoid loaded spinal flexion (no sit-ups, crunches, heavy bar-on-back squats, heavy conventional deadlifts, Jefferson curls). Use machines, hacked angles, goblet/landmine variants at modest loads, and unilateral work to keep spinal loads low.
- Bracing and hinge mechanics: Teach diaphragmatic breathing, 360° brace, hip hinge with minimal lumbar motion.
- Volume/progression: Start moderate volume, increase via reps, sets, and modest load jumps while observing pain-free range. RIR (reps in reserve) 2–3 early, 1–2 later.
- Exercise selection: Emphasize lower-body strength via split squats/lunges/step-ups, hip thrusts, hamstring curls; upper body via dumbbells, cables, machines; core via anti-flexion/anti-rotation/anti-extension.
- Tempo and control: 2–3 second eccentrics, controlled transitions; avoid end-range loaded spinal flexion/extension.

Session template (each day)
1) Dynamic warm-up (8–10 min)
- 3–5 min light cardio (bike, brisk walk, elliptical)
- Mobility/activation: cat-cow (gentle range), hip flexor half-kneeling stretch, thoracic rotation open-books, glute bridges (BW 2x12), dead bug (2x6/side), bird dog (2x6/side), bodyweight hip hinge patterning
2) Main lifts: 3–4 exercises
3) Assistance: 2–3 exercises
4) Core/conditioning finisher: 1–2 drills
5) Cool-down: easy cardio 3–5 min, breathwork

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and motor control. Technique, bracing, unilateral bases, machines, tempo.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive strength. Slight load increase, lower rep ranges, introduce more challenging variations (still low axial load).
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidation and performance. Heavier within constraints, power/tempo elements, slight volume deload week 9 then push.

Load guidance
- Use RIR. Week 1: 3 RIR; Week 2–3: 2 RIR; Week 4: 1–2 RIR (then small deload into Phase 2 as written below). Progress 2.5–5% load when all sets hit top reps with target RIR and no symptom provocation.
- Stop any set if pain > 3/10, sharp or radiating symptoms, or loss of neutral spine.

Week-by-week plan

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (Foundation, control, capacity)
Goal: Groove patterns, build tolerance, improve core stiffness, glute/ham strength, upper-body strength. Tempo 3-1-1 on most lifts.

Week 1
Day A
- Leg Press (feet mid-high, neutral spine): 3x10, 3 RIR
- DB Bench Press (flat): 3x10, 3 RIR
- Half-Kneeling Cable Row (neutral grip): 3x12/side
- Hip Thrust (barbell pad or Smith, light): 3x10
- Seated Hamstring Curl: 3x12
- Core: Pallof Press 3x10/side; Side Plank 3x20–30s/side

Day B
- Goblet Box Squat to parallel (box height to maintain lumbar neutrality): 3x8–10
- Lat Pulldown (neutral grip): 3x10
- DB Incline Press: 3x10
- Reverse Lunge (DBs, short step, upright torso): 3x8/side
- Cable Face Pull: 3x12–15
- Core: Dead Bug 3x6/side (slow); Bird Dog 3x6/side (slow holds)

Day C
- Landmine Hack Squat or Belt Squat (if available): 3x10
- Chest-Supported DB Row: 3x10
- Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift (contralateral DB, light): 3x8/side (hip hinge only, keep lumbar neutral)
- Seated Machine Shoulder Press (neutral grip): 3x10
- Leg Extension: 3x12
- Core: Tall-Kneeling Cable Anti-Extension (rollout trainer if very controlled) 3x8; Farmer Carry (2 DBs, short steps) 4x20–30m light-moderate

Week 2
- Keep exercises; add 1 set to first two compounds each day (e.g., 4 sets), keep RIR ~2–3.
- Add 5–10% load if Week 1 felt easy, or add 1–2 reps within ranges.

Week 3
- Progress load slightly (2.5–5%) on compounds; aim 2 RIR. Increase SLRDL to 3x9/side, hip thrust to 4x8–10.

Week 4
- Slight push before transitioning: main lifts 4x8–10 at 1–2 RIR; assistance unchanged.
- Swap one upper movement for variety:
  - Day A: Cable Chest Press (standing, split stance) 3x10
  - Day B: Single-Arm Cable Row (tall kneeling) 3x10/side
  - Day C: Machine Lateral Raise 3x12–15
- Core: progress holds to 30–40s; Pallof to 12–15 reps.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (Strength progression, low axial load)
Goal: Increase intensity modestly, lower reps on compounds, keep strict form. Introduce tempo pauses (1–2s at bottom on leg press, goblet squat). Farmer carries slightly heavier.

Week 5
Day A
- Leg Press: 4x6–8 (2 RIR, 2s pause at bottom)
- DB Bench Press: 4x6–8
- Hip Thrust: 4x6–8 (pause 1s at top)
- Chest-Supported Row: 3x8–10
- Hamstring Curl: 3x10
- Core: Pallof Iso Hold 3x20–30s/side; Suitcase Carry 4x20–30m (one DB, alternate)

Day B
- Belt Squat or Landmine Squat (light-moderate): 4x6–8
- Neutral-Grip Pull-Up or Assisted Pull-Up: 4x5–8
- DB Incline Press: 3x8
- Bulgarian Split Squat (DBs, shallow depth to neutral spine): 3x8/side
- Face Pull + External Rotation (cable) superset: 3x12 each
- Core: Dead Bug with band tension 3x8/side; Side Plank with top-leg abduction 3x20s/side

Day C
- 45° Back Extension (hip hinge focus, neutral spine, arms across chest; load only if perfect): 3x10–12 light
- Single-Leg Press (foot mid-high): 3x8/side
- Seated Machine Shoulder Press: 4x6–8
- One-Arm Cable Row (standing): 3x8–10/side
- Leg Extension: 3x10–12
- Core: Anti-Extension Wheel to wall or Cable Fallouts 3x8–10; Farmer Carry heavier 4x30–40m

Week 6
- Progress loads 2.5–5% on compounds if all sets hit top reps at 1–2 RIR.
- Add 1 set to Bulgarian split squat (now 4x8/side).
- Add a hamstring-dominant accessory: Seated or Lying Ham Curl 1 extra set (now 4x10).

Week 7
- Keep volumes; reduce reps to 5–7 on main lifts and raise load accordingly (maintain 1–2 RIR).
- Swap DB bench for Machine Chest Press for stability (4x5–7).
- Core: Add Half-Kneeling Lift/Chop 3x8/side.

Week 8
- Slight overreach: maintain Week 7 loads, add 1 set to first lower and first upper compound each day.
- Finishers: Light sled push/pull 4x20–30m if available (upright posture), or bike intervals 6x45s easy-hard.

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 (Consolidation, strength-endurance, power control)
Goal: Solidify strength, introduce safe power elements (med ball), maintain spine safety. Week 9 is a deload. Then progressive push Weeks 10–12.

Week 9 (Deload)
- Reduce volume ~40–50%. Keep technique crisp, 3 RIR.
Day A: Leg Press 3x6; DB Bench 3x6; Row 2x8; Core light holds 2x20s.
Day B: Belt/Landmine Squat 3x6; Assisted Pull-Up 3x5; Split Squat 2x6/side; Core 2 drills easy.
Day C: Hip Thrust 3x6; Shoulder Press 3x6; Single-Leg Press 2x8; Carries light 3x20m.

Week 10
Day A
- Leg Press: 5x5 (controlled, 1–2 RIR)
- Machine Chest Press or DB Bench: 4x5–6
- Chest-Supported Row: 4x6–8
- Hamstring Curl: 3x8–10
- Core: Pallof Press to Overhead (anti-extension) 3x8/side; Suitcase Carry heavy 4x30m

Day B
- Hip Thrust: 5x5 (pause 1s top)
- Neutral-Grip Pull-Up/Assisted: 5x4–6
- Bulgarian Split Squat: 4x6–8/side
- Landmine Press (half-kneeling): 3x6–8/side
- Face Pull: 3x12–15
- Power-safe: Med Ball Chest Pass (standing) 3x6–8 light-moderate
- Core: Side Plank 3x30–40s/side

Day C
- Belt Squat or Landmine Squat: 5x5
- One-Arm Cable Row: 3x8–10/side
- Seated Shoulder Press: 4x6
- Single-Leg RDL (light-moderate) or Slider Hamstring Curl if RDL not tolerated: 3x8/side
- Leg Extension: 3x10–12
- Power-safe: Med Ball Rotational Throw (tall-kneeling to wall) 3x6/side (control trunk; no lumbar twist)
- Core: Anti-Extension Rollout to comfortable range 3x8

Week 11
- Progress loads 2.5–5% if Week 10 felt solid; keep rep schemes.
- Add Step-Up (DBs, mid-shin to below-knee height) 3x8/side on Day C; remove leg extension that day to balance volume.
- Carries: Farmer Carry heavy 4x40m on Day A.

Week 12
- Test week within constraints (not 1RMs): pick one main lower and one main upper per day and perform a top set at RIR 1, then a back-off set.
Day A: Leg Press build to top set 5–7 reps @ RIR 1; back-off 2x6 at -10% load. Row 3x6–8; Ham Curl 3x8–10; Core/carry normal.
Day B: Hip Thrust top set 5–7 @ RIR 1; back-off 2x6 @ -10%. Pull-Up AMRAP perfect form leaving 1 rep in tank; Split Squat 3x6/side; Landmine Press 3x6–8; Med ball chest pass 3x6.
Day C: Belt/Landmine Squat top set 5–7 @ RIR 1; back-off 2x5 @ -10%. Seated Shoulder Press 3x5–6; Single-Leg RDL or Slider Curl 3x8; Rotational throw 3x6/side; Core rollout 3x6–8.

Conditioning, mobility, and desk-worker considerations
- Low-impact cardio 2–3x/week 20–30 min (incline treadmill walk, bike, elliptical).
- Daily mobility micro-breaks: every 45–60 min, 2–3 min standing, hip flexor stretch, thoracic extensions over chair back, gentle standing hamstring floss (no loaded spinal flexion).
- Optional dedicated mobility 2x/week: hip flexor/quad, glute/piriformis, adductor rocks, thoracic rotation, calf.

Core and bracing cues
- 360° brace: inhale through nose, expand lower ribs and abdomen circumferentially, light pelvic floor engagement; maintain during effort; exhale through sticking point without losing neutral.
- Hinge: soft knees, push hips back, maintain long spine, feel hamstrings load; stop before lumbar flexion.
- Avoid flexion-based ab work; prioritize anti-movement.

Exercise substitutions (if any discomfort)
- If single-leg RDL aggravates back: swap for slider leg curl, Nordic curl eccentrics (assisted), or hamstring curl variations.
- If belt squat unavailable: landmine squat, leg press emphasis, or goblet box squat kept moderate.
- If hip thrust uncomfortable: substitute glute bridge on bench, feet-elevated, or cable pull-through (light, hinge-neutral).

Progress tracking
- Log loads, reps, RIR, and any symptoms (time, movement, rating).
- Aim for steady 2.5–5% load bumps on compounds every 1–2 weeks if form and RIR targets are met symptom-free.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep: 7–9 hours/night. Consistent schedule.
- Walking: 7–10k steps/day if tolerable.
- Hydration: ~30–35 ml/kg/day.
- Nutrition (general, adjust to goals):
  - Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day.
  - Calories: slight surplus for strength/hypertrophy if desired (+150–250 kcal/day) or maintenance for recomposition.
  - Carbs around training: 30–60 g pre, 30–60 g post; include 20–40 g protein within 2 hours post-workout.
  - Omega-3s, fruits/veg (5+ servings/day), adequate calcium/vitamin D.
- Delayed onset soreness is okay; sharp back pain or radiating symptoms are not—regress and reassess.

Red flags and form boundaries
- No loaded spinal flexion (no crunches, sit-ups with plates, heavy RDLs to loss of neutral, toes-to-bar, etc.).
- No heavy axial loading (avoid back squats, heavy barbell deadlifts, heavy overhead barbell work).
- Keep ranges where lumbar neutrality is guaranteed; prioritize quality over load.

This plan builds general strength safely, focusing on lower-body capacity without heavy spinal loading, robust core anti-movement, and balanced upper-body work. Adjust loads and exercises based on the client’s weekly response while honoring the physio’s guidance.
